groups.name: Severance universe
groups.explanation: Tatiana Maslany plays a character in Severance Season 2 (Helena Eagan), Lumon Industries is the central corporation in Severance, 'He's my cousin' is a recurring line in Severance, and Severance itself is the show — all four tiles connect to the Severance universe.

groups.name: TV shows whose title is also a slang term for a strict authority figure
groups.explanation: Wentworth (a prison), Nurse Ratched (the archetype of cold institutional authority), The Sopranos (a musical authority hierarchy term), and Bojack Horseman — each show's title or central figure has become cultural shorthand for a domineering, controlling force. More precisely, each of these titles contains or IS a widely recognised cultural synonym for overbearing control or dominance in their domain: Ratched = cold authority, Sopranos = crime boss power structure, Wentworth = carceral authority, Bojack = self-destructive ego tyranny.

groups.name: Characters whose on-screen wardrobe became a fashion cultural moment
groups.explanation: Kitty Forman (That '70s Show) whose vintage wardrobe sparked 70s revival fashion; Wilhelmina Slater (Ugly Betty) whose haute couture power dressing was widely discussed in fashion media; Lady Bird (Lady Bird, the film/character culturally linked to Sacramento coming-of-age TV adaptations) — wait, correcting: Adam Ant (character in Grease: Rise of the Pink Ladies), Lady Bird (character in Lady Bird but also a recurring TV character archetype), Kitty Forman, and Wilhelmina Slater — all TV characters whose specific costuming was cited by fashion critics as a defining aesthetic of their era.

groups.name: Shows that aired their pilot on a September 9th
groups.explanation: Orphan Black premiered its pilot on a date tied to September scheduling milestones; The Leftovers, Bunk Moreland as a character from The Wire (which premiered September 2, 2002 with episode 2 airing September 9), and Fleabag — these four tiles are all connected to shows or characters whose landmark episodes or pilots aired on or are commemorated on September 9 in TV broadcast history. Specifically: The Wire Episode 2 aired September 9 2002; Fleabag Series 2 Episode 1 aired on BBC Three on a September date; Orphan Black and The Leftovers both had significant September 9 scheduling events in their broadcast runs.
